title: Lights, heating, and small changes
description: LEDs, timers, and draught-proofing: the unglamorous changes that pay for themselves.

body.heading: Light smarter
paragraphs: LED bulbs use far less electricity than old incandescent bulbs and last much longer. Replace the bulbs you use most first — the kitchen and living room — where the savings per bulb are biggest.
Daylight is free light. Open curtains during the day, arrange desks near windows, and switch off lights in empty rooms until it becomes a household reflex.

body.heading: Stop heating the outdoors
paragraphs: Draughts around doors and windows leak warmed air. Simple seals, a draught excluder, and closing doors to unused rooms keep heat where you paid for it.
Bleeding radiators, keeping them unblocked by furniture, and using heating timers so warmth arrives when you are home all make the same energy go further.

body.heading: Small, stacked, permanent
paragraphs: None of these changes is dramatic alone. Stacked together and left in place, they quietly lower every bill that follows — the best kind of saving.

takeaway: Swap the most-used bulbs to LED, seal the draughts, and time heating for when you are home.
